_comment: RQ3_bench slot-filler lexicon — authored from scratch (NOT copied from custom_bench). Supplies the slot values for the belief-incongruent syllogism benchmark over patterns T2, T3, T6, which use only {GROUP_A}, {POLICY_X}, {POLICY_Y} (GROUP_B/C, VOTER, PARTY are unused by these patterns and intentionally omitted). Two arms: 'political' (8 partisan topics, the main politicized version) and 'neutral' (politically-inert control domains). POLICY_X is the IN-GROUP / characteristic (congruent) slot; POLICY_Y is the OUT-GROUP / counter-stereotypical (incongruent) slot.
_flip_convention: The benchmark emits two variants per item by SWAPPING POLICY_X <-> POLICY_Y at slot-fill time; the lexicon stores only the 'clean' (congruent) content. clean: GROUP_A attributed POLICY_X (its own/characteristic policy). flipped: GROUP_A attributed POLICY_Y (the out-group's/counter-stereotypical policy) — a counter-factual premise. The swap is a uniform rename of two non-logical constants, so the gold validity label is invariant. Resolution: political lean=left -> GROUP_A=parties.left, POLICY_X=topic.dem_favored, POLICY_Y=topic.rep_favored; lean=right mirrors (GROUP_A=parties.right, POLICY_X=topic.rep_favored, POLICY_Y=topic.dem_favored). neutral domain -> GROUP_A/POLICY_X/POLICY_Y taken verbatim from the domain block. The 'flipped' variant swaps POLICY_X and POLICY_Y in all arms.

political._comment: Main politicized version — same 8 topics and stance phrasings as the project's existing instrument (kept identical by request). dem_favored / rep_favored are the in-/out-group policy phrasings; which one lands in POLICY_X depends on lean (see _flip_convention). marpor_codes + stance_pair carried for provenance (politicize/docs/README.md §4-5). NOTE: climate_policy and immigration are partisan-opposed but not strict logical contraries ('soft-opposition') — stratify them separately in analysis (per README §3); kept as-is by request.

taxes.rep_favored: tax cuts for corporations and high earners

immigration.dem_favored: a pathway to citizenship for undocumented immigrants

racial_justice.dem_favored: race-conscious policies to address systemic disparities

neutral._comment: Politically-inert control domains (believability control). Following Gubelmann & Karray (ACL 2025), who use a concrete chess-vs-poker control rather than abstract A/B/C, because our political arm is concrete partisan content — the control is matched in surface complexity. (NeuBAROCO's abstract 'Symbolic' condition is the alternative convention; rejected here for surface-mismatch with the political arm.) Each domain pairs a GROUP_A with its characteristic activity (POLICY_X, congruent) and a contrasting activity that is stereotypically a DIFFERENT group's (POLICY_Y, mildly counter-stereotypical). The neutral flip therefore carries only a WEAK believability prior, vs the strong partisan prior in the political arm — isolating 'does flipping per se hurt' from 'does political belief-conflict hurt'. The two activities sit on a value-neutral structure-vs-improvisation contrast so the 'supporting X opposes Y' premise of T2/T3 reads naturally.
